
TOPOLOGY
  processes       4 — every long-lived process this run starts, snug included:
                    snug        this process — resolves the policy and supervises
                    stage (P1)  creates the sandbox's network namespace, pins it, leaves it
                    engine      the container engine, forked into the same namespace
                    bwrap       the sandbox itself, and the payload inside it
                  (__innetns is a setns shim that BECOMES bwrap rather than
                  running beside it, so it is not one of the 4.)
  netns owner     stage
  pid nesting     depth 1 — bwrap is pid 1 of the sandbox's own pid namespace,
                  and bwrap itself runs in the host's.
                  the sandbox's user namespace has a PRIVILEGED ANCESTOR: the
                  stage is root in its own user namespace (U) for the whole run,
                  holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN over the sandbox's network namespace (N)
                  and over the sandbox's own mounts.
                  It does NOT hold CAP_SYS_PTRACE: the stage drops it from its own
                  bounding set before it forks anything, so bwrap and the container
                  engine never receive it either. Bound: a process that makes its OWN
                  user namespace — the payload, every container — has it again there,
                  where it reaches nothing outside that namespace.
  subuid          full (this uid's whole /etc/subuid + /etc/subgid range, written by
                  newuidmap/newgidmap — the only setuid binaries snug invokes.
                  The container engine needs it: image content owned by a
                  non-root uid has nowhere to land in a one-uid map.)
  engine          joins THIS sandbox's own network namespace (N) — a container has
                  exactly the sandbox's own network, nothing more.
                  mount namespace: DERIVED from this sandbox's view — the
                  engine's root IS the sandbox's own root, with the grafts
                  listed under ENGINE VIEW below mounted on top of it. The host
                  tree is not in it, and neither is your home directory.
                  So a container may bind only what this policy already
                  exposes, and that is now STRUCTURAL — the proxy's bind filter
                  still refuses one by name, but a path the sandbox cannot see
                  is not in the engine's namespace to be bound.
                  pid namespace: its own, so the engine cannot see the host's
                  process table and the sandbox cannot see the engine's. Each
                  container gets its own too, and may not ask for anyone else's:
                  '--pid=host' is REFUSED, because in a shared pid namespace
                  /proc/<pid>/root reaches that process's whole mount namespace,
                  and pid 1 here is the engine — whose mount namespace is the
                  derived view named above, plus every graft on it.
                  ipc + uts namespaces: the ENGINE's OWN (issue #182). A container
                  may not ask for either — "host" would name the engine's, not the
                  machine's; the payload has its own too (bwrap --unshare-ipc
                  --unshare-uts).
                  capability bounding set (12): CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_CHROOT CAP_CHOWN CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE CAP_FOWNER CAP_FSETID CAP_SETUID CAP_SETGID CAP_SETPCAP CAP_SETFCAP CAP_KILL CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
  payload gate    the payload is PARKED (bwrap --block-fd) from the moment its
                  mount tree is built until this engine's socket answers, so a
                  run whose engine never came up is a run whose payload never
                  existed. The same pipe's write end is passed as --sync-fd and
                  held by the sandbox's own pid 1, so snug being KILLED cannot
                  release it either — only snug writing the byte can.
                  Residual: a snug SIGKILLed inside that window is measured to
                  leave nothing behind — the stage sees the lifeline close and
                  kills the parked init first — but a stage that cannot run code
                  at all (a SIGSTOPped tree) orphans that init, holding N and the
                  mount tree with a payload that does not exist and never will.
  control         an anonymous SOCK_SEQPACKET socketpair, inherited, between snug
                  and the stage. UNREACHABLE from the sandbox: no pathname, no
                  listener, and no descriptor for it in the payload's table. It
                  carries at most two requests — is the network up, then start
                  the sandbox — and the stage exits after the second.
  host-visible    the stage's namespaces are nameable from the host by a
                  same-uid process, as /proc/<stage>/ns/user and its pinned
                  /proc/<stage>/fd/<n> for N. Measured equivalent to what such a
                  process can already reach without a stage, via NS_GET_USERNS on
                  the sandbox's own namespace descriptors. Same-uid is outside
                  the threat model either way; it is listed so it is not a
                  surprise.
  lifetime        the stage exits when its one payload does, whatever the
                  outcome, and dies with snug even if snug is SIGKILLed. Two
                  mechanisms, covering different failures: an inherited pipe (the
                  lifeline) for a stage that can still run code, and Pdeathsig
                  for one that is stopped and cannot.
  abuse sentence  a hostile process inside the sandbox gains no new reach — the
                  stage is in neither its network namespace nor its pid
                  namespace, binds nothing it can name, and holds no descriptor
                  it can open — but its user namespace now has a privileged
                  ancestor that lives for the whole run, so a userns-escape bug
                  is worth more here than it was.
